content: The Eisenhower Medical Center, located in Rancho Mirage, California, is the only not-for-profit hospital in the Coachella Valley. In 2005, it was recognized as one of the top 100 hospitals in the United States. The hospital is also home to the renowned Betty Ford Center. It operates as a General Acute Care Hospital and has provided Basic Emergency Services since 2006. The hospital is named after President Dwight D. Eisenhower, and its origins trace back to 1966 when entertainer Bob Hope was approached to lend his name to a charity golf tournament. The proceeds from this tournament were intended to fund the hospital's construction. Although Bob Hope's schedule prevented him from participating, he suggested that his wife, Dolores Hope, take on the role instead. Dolores Hope, a highly skilled and dedicated philanthropist, agreed and became deeply involved in the hospital's development. Since 1968, she has served as President, Chairman of the Board, and Chairman Emeritus, playing a pivotal role in every major decision regarding the hospital. The original 80 acres of land for the hospital were donated by Bob and Dolores Hope, who also spearheaded efforts to raise private funds for its construction. Numerous prominent figures from the entertainment and political worlds contributed their time to fundraising events and dedication ceremonies. The hospital's official records highlight the involvement of notable individuals such as Richard Nixon, Gerald Ford, Spiro Agnew, George H.W. Bush, Ronald Reagan, Frank Sinatra, George Burns, Bing Crosby, Gene Autry, and Lucille Ball. Two months after the groundbreaking ceremony in 1969, Dolores Hope established the Eisenhower Medical Center Auxiliary, which has since become one of the most successful volunteer organizations of its kind globally. Bob Hope served as the master of ceremonies for the hospital's opening in November 1971. During the opening, tributes were paid to local philanthropists, including Mr. and Mrs. Walter Probst, Mr. and Mrs. Peter Kiewit, and Mrs. Hazel Wright, with medical buildings named in their honor. Bob Hope also presided over the inauguration of the 47-bed Mamie Eisenhower Wing. The hospital underwent significant expansion during the 1980s, with the Hopes actively participating in every major event and opening despite their demanding schedules. Key developments during this period included the establishment of the Annenberg Center for Health Sciences, the Betty Ford Center, the Barbara Sinatra Children's Center, the Dolores Hope Outpatient Care Center, and the Uihlein Administration Building. By 1990, the hospital had performed its 3,000th open-heart surgery. The Hopes' tireless efforts in supporting the Eisenhower Medical Center earned them widespread recognition and numerous accolades, including a combined total of 60 honorary doctorates. In 1996, during the hospital's 25th anniversary, the Hopes were honored with the Eisenhower Centennial Award, the institution's highest distinction. In January 2006, the Eisenhower Medical Center gained international attention when President Gerald Ford was admitted for a 16-day treatment for pneumonia. Following his death on December 26, 2006, his body was taken to the hospital, where Betty Ford issued a press release confirming his passing. His body remained at the hospital until the commencement of funeral services on December 29.
